text:
maria: Thinking out loud — want to propose a new pattern for spot/preemptible handling for interactive + batch: 'eviction credits' + shifted off-peak queues + regional hedging. TL;DR: give interactive queues short-term buyout credits, staggered maintenance windows across regions, and route cold batch to heavily preemptible pools. Feedback?

dan: quick q — what are eviction credits?

maria: small idea: each customer/requesting job gets an 'eviction credit' budget (seconds) that we can spend to gracefully drain/hand off state before preemption. Credits are topped up on off-peak shifts and scaled by priority. Not literal money, just scheduler budget.

simon: interesting. How do you track that? prometheus?

maria: yes — track per-queue credit balance + recent interruptions. e.g. prom query: `sum(rate(spot_interruptions_total[5m])) by (region)` and a gauge `queue_eviction_credits{queue="interactive"}`.

jin: operationally how does that help latency SLOs?

maria: idea: when a spot instance gets an eviction notice, if queue has credits we: 1) mark node DoNotSchedule; 2) start fast pre-checkpoint or handoff (90s window); 3) if still needed, we attempt to migrate a subset to a hot pool or call a burst from reserved capacity. Credits get consumed proportional to graceful window used.

olivia: are we assuming cloud providers send 2 min notice? some give ~30s. need fallback.

maria: yes window is configurable per provider/region. default config: `graceful_window_seconds: 90`, fallback_deadline: 20s. We'll attempt fast checkpoint within that 20s if provider only gives 30s.

infra-bot: deploy-check — referenced config files: `scheduler/eviction-credit-policy.yaml` and `routing/region-hedge.json`

maria: sample policy (very rough):
```yaml
policy_name: eviction-credit-v1
queues:
  interactive:
    credit_rate: 5s_per_hour
    max_balance: 120s
    preempt_behavior: migrate_to_hot_pool
  batch:
    credit_rate: 0s_per_hour
    max_balance: 0s
    preempt_behavior: immediate_eviction
hot_pool:
  reserved_percent: 10
  burst_size: 5
```

dan: so hot_pool is reserved capacity (dedicated) we keep at ~10% and use for migrations? cost tradeoff?

maria: exactly. rough numbers from our test cluster: pinned/dedicated GPUs cost ~3.1x spot, but if we keep 10% reserved and use it to avoid failure for top-priority requests we reduce outrages by ~70% (measured on latency p99) for a 15% rise in overall spend. still net cheaper than overprovisioning.

simon: how do we do regional hedging? route-by-policy? what if region-wide maintenance hits multiple zones?

maria: route-by-policy + time-shifted maintenance. Hedge by ensuring a customer’s interactive traffic hits at least two regions spread across providers/zones where possible. Also schedule heavy noncritical batch jobs to run during the region's historical low-interruption window.

jin: need a simple gameplan to test this. small rollout idea?

maria: rollout plan:
- phase 0: simulate on staging with replayed traffic and synthetic evictions
- phase 1: enable credits for 10% of interactive traffic, keep migration to hot_pool as opt-in feature flag
- phase 2: expand to 50%, tune credit_rate and hot_pool size
- phase 3: global rollout + reporter dashboards

olivia: what about preemption spikes during large on-sale events? credits will be exhausted. fallback policy?

maria: fallback: when credits depleted, degrade to best-effort: 1) prefer live-migration to another spot in same region, 2) if not available, spill to batch queue (best-effort) or call dedicated burst if SLA-critical. We keep a small circuit-breaker that prevents unlimited burst to hot_pool.

dan: do we need new infra pieces? eviction webhook? controllers?

maria: yes small controller + admission webhook to track credit balances on job creation and consume on node-notice events. plus a light-weight checkpointing library for quick state dump.

simon: can we reuse existing eviction-handler? we have `eviction-collector` that logs notices. maybe extend it.

maria: good point — extend `eviction-collector` to forward to credit-controller.

infra-bot: perf-note — sample prometheus alerts to add: `queue_eviction_credits_low{queue="interactive"} for 5m` and `hot_pool_burst_rate > 0.5`

jin: what about fairness across tenants? big tenants might hog credits.

maria: credits top-up policy: proportional to last-30-day spend tier + a minimum baseline. We also enforce per-tenant max_balance and soft-penalties (rate-limiting) when they exceed.

olivia: sounds promising. one ask: include exact bookkeeping schema and example metrics in the staging run so SRE can run replay.

maria: will add to the RFC. I'll open a short PR with `scheduler/eviction-credit-policy.yaml` and a staging-run dashboard. Thanks for early feedback :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident-sim queued: simulate 10k evictions across us-west2/eu-west1 next tuesday 03:00 UTC — tag: infra-experiment

maria: perfect — that'll give us a real signal. anyone wants to join the run?

dan: I'll be oncall that window, can help watch migration errors.

simon: count me in for metrics and dashboards.

maria: cool — I'll share PR + playbook by end of day.
